title: Mara and the Inheritance
premise: Zephyrine Kavanagh, a night-shift dispatcher who has catalogued every death his town can offer, is dragged into an impossible case when the exhumed coffin of beloved founder Aldous Merrick is found empty. The trail leads through a thirty-year-old night when five friends wove alibis around a drowning at Graywater Cove — a night Zephyrine's own mother was part of. As the tide gives up bones, letters, and a second coffin, Zephyrine discovers the founder faked his death to protect the town from his own crime, and that the person digging him up is the daughter he abandoned. In the end, Zephyrine must choose between exposing the truth that will shatter his found family at the taxi company or burying it forever — and he finds a third way, letting the living testify while the dead stay at rest.
about_author: Lena Whitlock spent a decade answering phones for a coastal taxi company before turning to fiction, and her dialogue still carries the cadence of 3 a.m. radio chatter. She lives in a fog-bound harbor town where she keeps, she admits, an unseemly interest in old cemetery records.

chapters.title: The Night Shift Knows
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A quiet dispatch shift establishes the taxi company as a found family — gruff owner Dev, driver-sage Odette, rookie Tam. A call about the Merrick exhumation crackles over the radio, and Zephyrine feels the town's attention turn. Beat: uneasy curiosity.

chapters.title: Empty Oak
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. At the cemetery, the coffin is opened before a crowd: no founder, only river stones and a brass key. Zephyrine recognizes the key's tag as taxi-company property. Beat: the ordinary world cracks open.

chapters.title: Alibis, Thirty Years Dried
chapters.summary: Zephyrine interviews the aging notary who notarized five identical statements in 1994. Each swears Aldous Merrick died at home. The notary's hands shake when Zephyrine mentions Graywater Cove. Beat: dread beneath polite surfaces.

chapters.title: The Key That Shouldn't Fit
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The brass key opens a long-sealed company locker containing a driver's log from 1994 with one night torn out. Dev orders him to leave it alone. Beat: loyalty begins to strain.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Founder
chapters.summary: Isolde Merrick's POV. The founder's estranged daughter arrives from abroad, cold and precise, admitting she paid for the exhumation. She wants to know what her father buried. Beat: a rival investigator enters the game.

chapters.title: Graywater Cove
chapters.summary: Zephyrine walks the cove at low tide, finding a rusted chain eyelet in the rocks. A local fisher mentions a second coffin-sized crate hauled out one night in '94 — by taxi. Beat: the past acquires geography.

chapters.title: Five Friends
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He maps the five signatories: the notary, a retired judge, a hotelier, his own mother, and Dev. His mother's name lands like a blow; she died believing she'd kept a promise. Beat: personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: What Mother Left
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In his mother's effects he finds an unmailed letter: 'Aldous isn't dead. Don't let them dig. The tide keeps what it's paid for.' Beat: grief and betrayal braided together.

chapters.title: The Judge's Denial
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Isolde, uneasy allies, corner the retired judge. He recites the old alibi verbatim, word for word identical to the notary's — rehearsed. Beat: the conspiracy shows its seams.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Someone jams the dispatch line the night he plans to revisit the locker; the office is ransacked, the log gone. Only Tam saw a figure in a company coat. Beat: the family has a traitor.

chapters.title: Odette Remembers Driving
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. The old driver recalls her first week in '94, when she was told to wash salt water out of a company car's floorboards and never ask why. Beat: the found family's foundations tremble.

chapters.title: Isolde's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. She reveals her father vanished from her life years before his 'death' — she received money orders signed by a stranger. She suspects the coffin was empty from the day it was buried. Beat: motive sharpens into obsession.

chapters.title: The Hotelier's Ledger
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The hotelier, dying and unafraid, shows a 1994 ledger: Aldous Merrick checked in under a false name the week after his funeral. Beat: the founder lived.

chapters.title: What the Tide Paid For
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Dredging permits from '94 point to a drowned man — not Merrick, but Merrick's business partner, officially lost at sea. The alibis covered a killing, not a fake death. Beat: the mystery inverts.

chapters.title: Dev's Long Night
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The company owner confesses in fragments: he drove the crate that night, believing he was moving contraband for men he trusted. He has protected the secret ever since. Beat: a father figure falls from grace.

chapters.title: The Coat
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Tam identifies the ransacker's coat as belonging to the judge's grandson, a company driver. Confrontation goes wrong; the grandson flees into the fog. Beat: pursuit, first physical danger.

chapters.title: Letters in a Locker
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. She finds her father's unsent letters hidden in a second locker — he wrote to her for thirty years from a room above the harbor hotel, too ashamed to sign. Beat: tenderness inside the crime.

chapters.title: The Man Upstairs
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The hotel room above the harbor is preserved, dust-sheeted, lived-in until weeks ago. On the desk: the torn log pages and a confession addressed 'To whoever finds the cove empty.' Beat: the dead man speaks.

chapters.title: Aldous's Confession
chapters.summary: Aldous's letter, read in Zephyrine's voice. His partner died in a struggle over embezzled town funds; Aldous staged his own death so the town's myth — and his daughter's inheritance — would survive. Beat: sympathy for the guilty.

chapters.title: Someone Else Read It First
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The confession's second copy is missing. The grandson has it, and he's blackmailing the judge and notary — or worse, planning to finish what the cove started. Beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A spring storm is forecast; the fisher warns the cove will give up or swallow everything in one tide. Isolde insists they dive the eyelet chain before it's too late. Beat: nature becomes a deadline.

chapters.title: The Notary Breaks
chapters.summary: The notary's POV. Terrified by blackmail, she confesses the alibi was written by the judge, and that the five friends each believed the others were guilty of the partner's death. Beat: the conspiracy's mutual hostage-keeping exposed.

chapters.title: Under the Eyelet
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Isolde dive at slack tide, finding the crate — empty, lid pried, chains cut recently. The grandson got there first. Beat: hope stolen at the last moment.

chapters.title: Blood on the Radio
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Dispatch receives a garbled distress call from the grandson's taxi; his car is found abandoned at the cove road, confession copy gone from the seat. Beat: fear that the secret is killing again.

chapters.title: The Judge's Bargain
chapters.summary: The judge offers Zephyrine a deal: silence in exchange for the company's survival — he'll bury the case and enrich Dev's fleet. Zephyrine refuses. Beat: love against duty crystallizes.

chapters.title: What Odette Kept
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. She produces the thing she never reported: a 1994 photo of the five friends on the cove road — and a sixth figure, young, holding the flashlight. The judge's son. Beat: a new suspect surfaces.

chapters.title: The Sixth at the Cove
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The judge's son died young, officially of accident — but the grandson has been researching his father's death for years. His blackmail was never about money. Beat: motive reframed as grief.

chapters.title: Isolde's Choice
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Offered the town's silence and her father's restored name if she abandons the investigation, Isolde instead publishes the letters — her inheritance is truth, not reputation. Beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Tide Turns
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Storm peak. The cove surrenders its last secret: the partner's remains, and with them evidence the death was struggle, not murder — and that the judge's son died trying to confess it. Beat: exculpation and horror together.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Meeting
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The grandson, half-drowned, is found alive in the old lighthouse with his father's confession. He never meant harm; he meant to make the judge say one true sentence. Beat: climax of confrontation, not violence.

chapters.title: One True Sentence
chapters.summary: The judge's POV. On the cove road before the town, the judge admits the alibi, the cover-up, and his son's despair. He surrenders the rehearsed words forever. Beat: catharsis through confession.

chapters.title: What the Law Allows
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Prosecutors weigh a thirty-year-old cover-up against the partner's accidental death. Aldous, if alive, would face little; the judge, everything. Dev faces losing his license. Beat: justice proves imperfect.

chapters.title: The Room Above the Harbor
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Isolde search the hotel room together and find a final letter: Aldous, dying of illness, watched the exhumation news and walked into the sea he'd used twice. Beat: the founder's true ending, quiet and sad.

chapters.title: The Second Coffin
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The partner is buried properly; Aldous's empty coffin is sealed with the river stones and Isolde's letters inside. The town chooses its myth knowingly. Beat: ritual, mourning, release.

chapters.title: Dev Steps Down
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. He sells the company to Odette and Tam, keeping only his old route. Zephyrine drives him home — dispatcher and driver, roles reversed. Beat: the found family reshapes without breaking.

chapters.title: The Notary's Peace
chapters.summary: The notary burns the five alibis with the families present, each reading one aloud first. Some forgive; some don't come. Beat: the cost of thirty years counted honestly.

chapters.title: Night Shift, Again
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Back at dispatch, the radio is just a radio. Tam asks what he learned from all of it. Zephyrine: 'That every death has a night shift too — someone keeping watch over it.' Beat: wisdom earned, gently delivered.

chapters.title: Isolde Stays
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. She buys the harbor hotel and keeps her father's room as it was, door open to the town. She and Zephyrine share a first careful dinner — love beginning where the investigation ends. Beat: warmth after ruin.

chapters.title: The Tide's Ledger
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Final walk at Graywater Cove. He buries his mother's unmailed letter at the eyelet, keeps the brass key, and watches the water take and give nothing more. Beat: acceptance, the mystery at rest.

chapters.title: Mara and the Inheritance
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Odette's POV. The company's new night dispatcher — a young woman everyone calls Mara — asks Zephyrine about the brass key on his chain. He tells her the truth, all of it. Some inheritances are meant to be carried in the open. Beat: the story passes on; found family endures.
